newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia April palm oil output seen up six pct.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia April palm oil output seen up six pct.

text.p: Malaysia's palm oil output in April is expected to rise six percent to 723,000 tonnes over March, crop forecaster Ivan Wong said on Monday.
Exports in April are estimated to increase by 40,000 tonnes over March exports of 565,219 tonnes.
Wong expects palm oil stocks at the end of April at 695,000-705,000 tonnes, compared with the Palm Oil Registration and Licensing Authority's (PORLA) 689,633 tonnes at end-March.
Wong said in a report that production remained good in the first half of April with output of major producers/millers ranging from unchanged to up 15 percent.
The rise in output was again likely to be matched by increases in offtake, Wong said.
"We thus expect end-April stocks of palm oil to be little changed," he said.
Wong said the tight supply of crude palm oil continued into April because of a big reduction in arrival of oil from eastern Sabah state.
